transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-28
Start: 09:32 PT
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Alicia Rivera (Redwood AE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Redwood CSM), Lars Erikson (HavenHealth VP Eng), Priya Menon (HavenHealth SRE), Tom Caldwell (HavenHealth CTO), Becky Zhou (HavenHealth Infra)

Summary:
Quick handoff of the long-tail degradation drill, review of incident timeline, finalize playbook edits and owners, agree on bench and follow-up workshops. Focus on fallback routing, KV cache warmup, and audit log ask for compliance team.

Topics:
- Incident timeline recap and best-guess RCA
- Short vs long-tail degradations and circuit breaker behavior
- Fallback model variants and quantization tradeoffs
- Runbook edits, alert thresholds, on-call playbook
- Compliance/logging/KMS questions

Action items (recap in meeting):
- Send consolidated runbook and logs export (Alicia)
- Customer to run degradation in staging and provide traces (Priya)
- SE to prepare fallback model perf matrix and configs (Jon)

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia Rivera: All right thanks everyone for joining, uh 9:32 PT, quick agenda: we wanna walk the drill results, close owners, and make sure the playbook has the exact thresholds for your on-call.
[00:12] Lars Erikson: yeah thanks Alicia, um this was a bit of a shock, the long tail errors started after we had a traffic spike on Monday, the p99 increased slowly and then we had cascade retries, multiple downstreams, so uh first question i guess is — did the KV cache lose warm state or was cache invalidation the cause.
[00:28] Jon Park: my read from the logs you sent is that there were a couple of eviction storms, the KV cache got churned when the sequence length jumped and that caused extra tokenization and longer token latencies; also we saw batching windows spike so small requests got batched suboptimally. there's also one place where the model fallback didn't trigger quickly because the routing policy was still pinned to the high-accuracy pool.
[00:46] Priya Menon: just to clarify — that fallback pinned to high-accuracy pool, is that the reserved Dedicated pool or the Hosted fallback? we have both configured so need to be clear.
[00:54] Alicia Rivera: great callout. For HavenHealth currently you have a dedicated pool for baseline traffic and an auto-burst to hosted for overage. During the event the auto-burst threshold was hit but the routing policy had a hard pin to the dedicated high-accuracy model until we hit the per-minute failure threshold — which delayed the cheaper fallback. so there was a policy gap.
[01:12] Tom Caldwell: memory — are we seeing any OOM or GPU mem reclaiming? because we saw one pod restart around 03:14.
[01:19] Jon Park: the pod restart was due to a driver bump, we saw transient mem reclaim logs; not a hard OOM. But the restarts did evict caches, which made the warmed KV less effective. so sequence: burst -> batching skew -> pod restart -> cache cold -> p99 climb -> delayed fallback.
[01:33] Becky Zhou: hmm okay, makes sense. the thing I want is: can we get a documented pre-bake / warmup before traffic surges? some kind of proactive warmup hooks?
[01:41] Alicia Rivera: yes we have two parts: 1) prefix/KV cache prewarming (we can seed with typical prefixes), 2) request shaping to avoid massive simultaneous cache invalidations. we'll add a pre-bake job example to the runbook.
[01:53] Lars Erikson: and what about circuit breaker behavior — we saw retries pile up, it made downstream backpressure worse.
[02:00] Jon Park: right, so our recommended playbook: set a soft p95 latency threshold to kick in partial fallback, set a hard p99 to trigger full fallback and autoscaling; also configure retry budget on the client side so retries are rationed. we can give you the exact config snippets.
[02:16] Priya Menon: can you share the exact thresholds you recommend? because our compliance folks will require numbers.
[02:21] Jon Park: recommended starting point for HavenHealth workload: p95 350ms token latency -> partial fallback (lower capacity model), p99 900ms -> full fallback and scale-up. those numbers are somewhat workload dependent, we wanna validate in your stage bench.
[02:36] Alicia Rivera: and we'll include both the routing policy JSON and a canary rollout example so ops can rehearse.
[02:43] Tom Caldwell: on the compliance side — audit logs and KMS: our security team wants end-to-end proof that request ids map to logs and that keys are customer-managed.
[02:53] Maya Singh: quick note — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integration; we also produce audit trails tied to request ids, but sometimes the log IDs get munged in output. we'll share the mapping doc.
[03:05] Priya Menon: we saw a gap — the request id attached to the upstream service didn't appear in the same span in the Redwood logs, made correlation hard.
[03:12] Jon Park: that was likely because of a log sampling rule on the gateway during the spike; we will propose a tighter sampling config for your critical routes.
[03:19] Lars Erikson: ok. on the long tail mitigation — can you explain the small-model fallback tradeoffs? we care about correctness for clinical outputs.
[03:28] Jon Park: sure. small-model fallback reduces per-token latency and lowers chance of runaways, but you can see a drop in hallucination guardrails. for clinical content we'd recommend a guard process: route to small model + post-filtering classifier or prompt post-check. the other option is quantized variants of your main model which maintain quality but lower GPU mem. quantization can be tricky — some token embeddings behave slightly differently.
[03:50] Priya Menon: do you have benchmarks for 8-bit quant vs float16 for our 7B style model?
[03:55] Jon Park: yes. we'll attach a perf matrix; quick numbers off head: float16 p95 ~340ms, int8 quant p95 ~220ms but p99 behavior needs exercise because of occasional jitter. we'll share the detailed spreadsheet.
[04:09] Becky Zhou: can we also talk about network egress and region routing? we saw latency step-changes when requests flowed to a different region during the spike.
[04:17] Alicia Rivera: region routing issue is important — we noted a misroute to a secondary region due to a stale health check. we'll include a health-check tuning section in the playbook and recommend sticky routing for sessions where you need consistent model context.
[04:31] Tom Caldwell: is sticky routing compatible with KV caching?
[04:35] Jon Park: yes, sticky session + local KV cache is actually best for context-heavy flows; the downside is you can get hot-shard problems so we recommend a blended approach: shard by customer id but allow limited overflow with cache-resumption policies.
[04:49] Priya Menon: one more ops question: how do we verify fallback happened during an incident? our audit team wants an evidentiary trail.
[04:57] Maya Singh: we'll show the logs you can search for: routing_decision, model_variant, and a trace id that ties to model latency. we'll add a short kibana query in the runbook.
[05:06] Alicia Rivera: okay let's walk through the draft playbook line-by-line, quick. Page 1: incident detection thresholds, page 2: automated routing, page 3: manual escalation to SE.
[05:15] [crosstalk]
[05:20] Alicia Rivera: first line, detection: we recommend an aggregated signal combining p95 token latency and error-rate change over a 2-minute rolling window. does that align?
[05:28] Priya Menon: yes that fits our on-call tooling. we'll have a pager rule for p95 and a separate slack alert for p99.
[05:34] Lars Erikson: the tricky bit is what to do before fallback: do we automatically throttle or try to scale up? we saw scaling take too long last time.
[05:42] Jon Park: mix approach: immediate partial fallback to smaller variant for a grace period (30s) while we trigger scale-up. that prevents a cascade while infra catches up.
[05:52] Tom Caldwell: okay, can we have an automated kill-switch if retries > X per minute to stop hammering downstream?
[05:59] Jon Park: yes that's the retry budget idea — set per-client quotas and global throttles. we'll provide sample configs.
[06:07] Becky Zhou: i have a note — logging retention for forensics: we need 90-day raw request logs for regulatory pre-review. is that possible?
[06:14] Maya Singh: yes, but for hosted we store 30 days by default; for HavenHealth we can enable extended retention under an add-on or for Private. we'll include options and cost estimates in the doc Alicia sends.
[06:26] Priya Menon: regarding the bench — we plan to run a synthetic ramp plus randomized prompt sets that mimic our busiest endpoints. can Redwood provide the routing policy hooks to flip models mid-run?
[06:36] Jon Park: yes, we have a routing policy API and a feature flag for mid-run swaps, plus a safe rollback. we'll demo in the bench session.
[06:44] Alicia Rivera: quick commercial note — if you want guaranteed p99 targets, Dedicated reserve with inline SLAs is the path; otherwise hosted with routing controls gives most flexibility.
[06:54] Lars Erikson: we'll need an estimate of cost delta between the two for our Q4 planning.
[06:58] Alicia Rivera: we'll include a ballpark delta in the follow-up.
[07:02] Priya Menon: can I ask about artifact references — where will the runbook live?
[07:06] Alicia Rivera: we'll put the runbook in your shared S3 link and also in the Redwood Console -> Playbooks area. link will be shared in follow-up.
[07:14] Tom Caldwell: anything else on security? our compliance team also wants SSO mapping and RBAC examples.
[07:19] Maya Singh: we have SAML/SCIM mappings and role templates; we'll attach a sample mapping for HavenHealth that shows how to limit model change privileges.
[07:27] Priya Menon: perfect.
[07:30] Alicia Rivera: ok time check — we have about 30 minutes left, Jon can you run through the proposed bench plan?
[07:37] Jon Park: yep. Step 1: import your production-ish traces into staging, Step 2: run 3 ramp scenarios: slow leak, sudden spike, and sustained plateau; Step 3: run fallback-only test where we intentionally pin the main pool to simulate capacity pressure and observe p95/p99 of variants. we'll capture traces and the routing_decision logs.
[07:58] Lars Erikson: how long will each bench scenario take?
[08:01] Jon Park: each scenario 20-30 minutes with warmups; total ~2 hours including analysis so we'll schedule a separate 2-hour session.
[08:09] Priya Menon: fine, schedule it with Ops and we'll invite Security.
[08:13] Alicia Rivera: action owners recap: Alicia share doc + logs by Friday, Jon prepare fallback matrix and bench plan, Priya run staging degradation and upload traces. any blockers?
[08:22] Becky Zhou: one small blocker — we need a sample pre-bake job that doesn't trigger compliance alarms, i.e., it mustn't send PHI to Redwood.
[08:31] Jon Park: understood — we'll provide a synthetic pre-bake script that uses non-PHI placeholder prompts and still mirrors distribution.
[08:38] Priya Menon: great. also can we add a low-cost monitoring hook — a synthetic probe that runs every 5 minutes to detect cache melt?
[08:46] Jon Park: yep, a lightweight probe works; we'll include sample Grafana queries.
[08:51] Tom Caldwell: i'd like to emphasize evidence chain — can we also get a signed attestation of config changes after an incident for our auditors?
[08:58] Maya Singh: we can offer change history exports and signed audit snapshots for Private; for hosted we'll provide detailed audit logs and change events but signature support is an add-on. we'll call that out.
[09:10] Alicia Rivera: ok last thing — escalation email template, we'll add to runbook so your on-call can follow steps verbatim.
[09:17] [background chatter/typing]
[09:24] Alicia Rivera: all right thanks everyone. quick recap and I'll shoot the runsheet + runbook link, Jon will prep the bench matrix, Priya will run staging and we'll reconvene after bench.
[09:34] Lars Erikson: thanks all.
[09:36] Priya Menon: thanks, bye.
[09:37] Alicia Rivera: bye.
